newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia on road to recovery with new global ties.
newsitem.headline: Iberia on road to recovery with new global ties.

text.p: Spanish flagship airline Iberia said on Monday it was on its way to becoming one of the world's major airlines after setting two key international alliances last week.
"There is no reason we cannot be among the major players," Iberia Chairman Xabier de Irala told a news conference.

Iberia, on the verge of collapse just two years ago due to high costs and souring Latin American investments, on Friday signed long-promised preliminary deals with British Airways and U.S-based American Airlines.
The commercial deals, which foresee the establishment of code-sharing, frequent-flyer programmes and cargo operations among others, are part of Iberia's long-term recovery plan.
"The overriding objective is the consolidation of positive results," Irala said, adding that results continue to improve.
First-half net profit rose to 5.12 billion pesetas compared to a loss in 1996 of 1.79 billion pesetas, he said.
Iberia ended 1996 with a profit of 3.5 billion pesetas and said in February it expected to make a profit of 11 billion pesetas in the entire year.
"This is the first day of a new stage to make Iberia a great company," said Pedro Ferreras, chairman of state holding company SEPI, which controls Iberia.

Irala said the group had fulfilled all the commitments it made when the European Union approved in December 1995 an emergency state cash injection of 87 billion pesetas to save Iberia from bankruptcy.
The group agreed at the time to rid itself of the bulk of its Latin American holdings.
Within the American Airlines deal, Iberia will keep 10 percent of Aerolineas Argentinas which is its remaining holding in Latin America, and American Airlines will buy 10 percent of the group.
Aerolineas Argentinas narrowed its first-half losses this year to $12.8 million compared with $38 million in the year-earlier period. Its total debt is $4.24 million.
